 Early voting to expand in Cook County suburbs, Chicago wards Monday 
 Early voting will expand Monday to Chicago's 50 wards and in the suburbs for the midterm election. By Lissette Nuñez Monday, October 19, 2026 10:45AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google COOK COUNTY, Ill. (WLS) -- Early voting will expand Monday to Chicago's 50 wards and in the suburbs for the midterm election.
 Monday, Chicago election officials are expected to highlight accessibility and languages services for voters.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Officials also shared detail on a new technology over the weekend that will make ballot tracking more detailed.
 Cook County officials said the new software will better allow them to see when voters check in, monitor polling place activity, and flag locations that may need attention.
 RELATED | 2026 midterm elections: Voter information in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin 
 These are different ways the county hopes to make the voting process more efficient and transparent.
 "What's good for the public is they have confidence where that mail ballot is going. all the way down to our carrier route and back to our office," Cook County Deputy Clerk for Elections Ed Michalowskisaid. "What's good for the public is they have confidence where that mail ballot is going. all the way down to our carrier route and back to our office."
 In Illinois, some races to watch include the U.S. Senate, several congressional seats, Illinois governor and the first fully elected Chicago School Board.
 Monday, Faith leaders will also host a march to the polls in Bronzeville to highlight the expansion of early voting.
